title: Reading a workflow JSON like a map

questions.q: In the context of a ComfyUI workflow JSON, what does the reference tuple [N_j, k] inside a node's inputs field signify?
options: The data value stored in slot k of node N_j
The ID of the source node (N_j) and the index of the output slot (k) from which data is drawn
The execution order of node N_j followed by node k
The visual coordinates of node N_j on the canvas
questions.answer: The ID of the source node (N_j) and the index of the output slot (k) from which data is drawn
questions.why: The lesson states: 'For a given input slot S in node N_i, the value is a reference tuple: [N_j, k]. N_j is the ID of the source node. k is the index of the output slot on node N_j from which the data is drawn.'

questions.q: What are the two conditions that must hold for a workflow topology to be considered valid?
questions.answer: Existence (the referenced node N_j must exist in the workflow) and Slot Validity (the source node N_j must have an output slot at index k).
questions.why: The lesson explicitly lists these two conditions: '1. Existence: For every reference [N_j, k] in any node’s inputs, the node N_j must exist in W. 2. Slot Validity: The source node N_j must have an output slot at index k.'

questions.q: Why does the ComfyUI engine fail if a workflow contains a cycle (e.g., Node A feeds Node B, which feeds Node A)?
options: The JSON parser cannot handle recursive dictionaries
The engine cannot determine the execution order
The GPU runs out of memory during the loop
The visual interface fails to render the wires
questions.answer: The engine cannot determine the execution order
questions.why: The lesson explains: 'If you create a cycle... the engine cannot determine the execution order, and the workflow fails.'

questions.q: According to the lab results, what does the output 'RESULT link_target = 5' prove about the workflow topology?
options: Node 5 is the first node to be executed
The SaveImage node (ID 7) is correctly linked to the VAEDecode node (ID 5)
The data flow from Node 5 to Node 7 is corrupted
questions.answer: The SaveImage node (ID 7) is correctly linked to the VAEDecode node (ID 5)
questions.why: The lesson states: 'This proves that the SaveImage node (ID 7) is correctly linked to the VAEDecode node (ID 5). The variable ref_node_id extracted from the SaveImage inputs is 5.'

questions.q: What is the primary difference between the visual interface's 'wires' and the underlying JSON structure?
questions.answer: The visual interface shows lines representing connections, while the JSON contains references (addresses) to source nodes and slots, not the data itself.
questions.why: The lesson states: 'In the visual interface, you see a line from Node A to Node B. In the JSON, you don’t see a line. You see a reference... It does not contain the data itself; it contains the address of where to get the data.'
